The food is good, generous, and offers many Cuban specialties. The best thing is to let yourself be tempted and try several to discover the different flavors of the local cuisine.

A very nice place to visit during a trip to Little Havana.

To truly experience Cuban Miami, you will need to have a dining experience. We chose to eat our last meal of the vacation here while visiting the sites of Calle Ocho. While there are several great places to eat Cuban food, this is the best combination of food, drinks and music in the heart of Little Havana. 

The restaurant is a small building adjacent to Domino Park. While the building is small with a bar, stage and some 2 top seating, there is a courtyard behind with ample seating. We got reservations for 6, largest party at 11:30 and quickly had our table. When we were then helped by a great waitress that help us find the best things on the menu and everything was good. Situated in the center of the commercial area of Little Havana neighborhood, this restaurant/bar delivers on many levels but unfortunately underperforms on food quality. There is live music in the front area where the bar is located, as well in the back area which is a semi outdoor garden. The wonderful music masks the unspectacular food which was mediocre and generally overpriced. The fried fish Cuban sandwich, a staple of the county’s cuisine, was bland and served on an unremarkable bun. The shrimp “stew” was disappointing and overpriced, the black bean soup, ordinary. Old Havana is known for its drinks, the many varieties of Mojito do not disappoint… you would be better served to go visit for a cocktail and the live music and choose one of the many restaurant options close by for lunch or dinner.

Great Cuban food and service in the heart of Little Havana
Jun 2024 • Couples
We were in Little Havana in Miami on sad business which we concluded at lunch time. We always try to have Cuban food before leaving the area and there are few places (if any) to have better Cuban food than Southwest Miami. My brother looked up nearby restaurants and Old's Havana popped up with a very high rating, so off we went.
Only five minutes away but on a different plane of existence as the area is highly sought out by tourists galore; it was located next to "domino park.' The neighborhood had other restaurants, cigar stores, and tour buses!!! Old's has a parking lot at the rear of the restaurant, somewhat hidden, but accessible and free before 6pm. If you use the lot you can enter through the back of the restaurant and skip the crowds out on the sidewalk; save that for later.
First things first. Having lived in Miami a long time and experienced the haughtiness of servers who like to ignore your English we were surprised that almost the entire wait staff spoke excellent English. Didn't matter, I speak fluent Spanish.
The restaurant is open air with an air conditioned area up front but not cold. We sat here across from the bar. The restaurant is also known as "La Casa del Mojito." 
my wife ordered a passion fruit mojito from our very capable, friendly server, Marisabel.
For lunch we did not deviate from our usual, Vaca Frita for her Ropa Vieja for me; both dishes can be the standard by which a Cuban restaurant should be judged. Accompanied by maduros (fried plantains) and Yuca con Mojo (cassava with a garlic sauce, some places skimp on the sauce but not here).
We shared a flan, a creme caramel dessert and Cafe Cubano (for me, not shared). 
Word of caution: service fee of 18% was automatically added to the bill. Marisabel's work ethic and easy manner was well worth this and more.
We expected so-so food once we saw the hawkers out front trying to get people in but would go back anytime. Not a small place and lots of good food and drinks.

This is the best Cuban food I've had, period. That's why I eat here when I'm in town, often before Miami Marlins games (as the stadium is a mile up the street). I had the whitefish with moro rice and sweet plantains and all were outstanding as always.

But a few detractors to be aware of; the place is packed, loud, and uncomfortable. There are no free refills on drinks; you pay $4 for a soda and they just give you a 237 mL bottle and that's it! (Would have been cheaper at the game). Service is typically slow because they are so busy. AND they automatically charge you an 18% service fee so remember when you go to pay that the tip was already included.

The inside is too closely packed and uncomfortable for my tastes so I've started sitting outside. Even in the hot Miami summer, it's comfortable outside because there is a lot of shade and they do a good job with the fans. 

If you want a quiet dinner, not the place. If you want to get in and out with an inexpensive meal, not the place. But if you want phenomenal authentic Cuban food, it is definitely your place!

Servers are friendly and very helpful if you are first timers eating Cuban food like we were. I got the beef with sautéed onions and my husband got the fried flank steak, both were delicious. I loved the sweet fried plantain, which was like a fried chunk of sweet potato. The fries are crisp and come in a little wire basket and is a good portion. The black beans are good. We did not try the cocktails, but I had a Coke which they bring in a glass bottle and pour into a glass of ice. There is an 18% service charge, which is split among all the servers, but if you tip on top of that, your server gets to keep all of it (we tipped $10 because she was terrific). Spent about $60 before the tip. Overall, great value and delicious!
